title: Effectiveness of the perpetrator-focused program "Responsible Behavior with Younger Children" (3VK) for the prevention of sexual boundary violations by adolescents towards peers and younger children in German schools: A randomized controlled trial.
summary: The study uses a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to test the effectiveness of the 3VK intervention for the prevention of sexualized violence in schools. The intervention consists of a five-part teaching program (45 minutes per unit) that uses interactive methods to sensitize 6th and 7th grade students to topics such as consent, boundaries and responsible behavior towards younger children and peers. The teachers and specialists who implement the program receive specific training in advance to prepare them for teaching the content. The RCT design provides for the random allocation of schools into two groups: an intervention group that receives the program directly and a waiting list control group that undergoes the curriculum in the following school semester. In order to measure the effectiveness of the intervention, questionnaires are used before and after implementation to record self-efficacy, norms, attitudes and behavioural intentions. In addition, the teachers document any deviations from the planned implementation in order to take this into account in the analysis.
conditions: Sexual boundary violations by adolescents against their peers and younger children

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Pupils in sixth and seventh grade who are capable of giving their consent, who attend a mixed-gender class at one of the participating German mainstream schools, who are fluent in German and whose legal guardians have consented to their participation in the program and the data collection are included.
Exclusion criteria:
Students are excluded if they do not agree to participate in the program and the data collection or if they do not have the written consent of their legal guardians.
